Night City captivates you from the very first moment. The immersion, the lighting, and the sheer vertical aesthetic of this world remain unrivaled in the gaming landscape. And yet, after spending countless hours in its urban canyons, one is left with a deeply conflicted impression. Cyberpunk 2077 is a game full of contradictions: breathtaking yet frustrating, brilliant in its gameplay at times, yet at its core a monument to broken promises.

In terms of performance, the game now presents a pleasingly solid showing. Frame rates remain stable, and the graphical foundation is undoubtedly at the cutting edge of what modern hardware can achieve. All the more baffling, then, is a critical technical shortcoming: there are simply no native anti-aliasing settings. Players who rely on upscaling technologies - such as using FSR 3.1 at Quality setting - are confronted with extremely distracting flickering and unsightly image edges. The persistent shimmering and jaggies on fine geometry and textures cannot be corrected, as CD Projekt Red denies players control over traditional anti aliasing, it only forces TAA in background. It is a technical oversight that repeatedly and noticeably mars the visual enjoyment of an otherwise beautiful game world.
Native AA is unplayable, even on my hardware and RT on medium without redlection.

In terms of storytelling, the main plot centering on V is by no means disastrous - it is simply okay. Yet, it falls far short of the narrative brilliance found in The Witcher 3. The cyberpunk setting offers immense depth regarding social commentary, technology, and the darker sides of human nature, yet the game barely scratches the surface. Paradoxically, the biggest narrative misstep involved the most prominent figure of all: Johnny Silverhand. The focus on Keanu Reeves - and the sheer amount of screen time his character demanded - effectively sidelined V as a character. [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] completely blew me away because it flips the classic [i]"die young in a flash of glory"[/i] trope on its head—it’s a deeply personal story about [b]true autonomy[/b], surviving on your own terms, and facing the heavy weight of your choices without relying on cheap fairy-tale endings. Cleaning out entire rooms from the shadows was just ridiculously satisfying. My only real gripe is how the game almost forces you to start a whole new playthrough from scratch just to experience different story branches and get full replayability, but as a complete package, it's easily one of the most compelling gaming experiences out there.

Absolutely phenomenal game in 2026. But first, the journey.... I preordered this in 2020 and was ready for it at launch, but as we all know that was a complete shitshow release. Bugs, stability, performance, poor graphics, everything. I shelved it and didn't give it a chance until 2023 when the v2.0 update dropped.  But I didn't do as the devs recommended and start a fresh save. I loaded into a legacy one and still had horrible performance issues; this was on an RTX 3070 which was current at the time - not sure if save game related or hardware.

Shelve it again until this year, and several more updates later (now v2.31) I give it a go on a fresh save file, new class, and dropped it to Easy instead of Normal (i just wanna vibe with the story). And just WOW WHAT A NIGHT & DAY DIFFERENCE. The game finally looks gorgeous (Ray Tracing and Path Tracing updates, improved HDR), runs smooth as hell, zero crashes. I can finally get immersed in the story and open world and it has been addicting to say the least. Hell i've spent more time just exploring, both on foot and car, stumbling across random NPC encounters that will hook my curiousity and pull me down a dark alley and next thing I know I'm unlocking a new sidegig, wiping out a gang, finding easter eggs, or just finding a beautiful scenery to switch on Photo Mode and pose some characters. There is truly so much to do and i've barely scratched the surface w/ the 50 or so hours on this new file, plus there's the Phantom Liberty expansion which everyone tells me is just as good if not better than the base game! I'm looking forward to continuing to plow through this gem.

Cyberpunk 2077 is, in my opinion, the best story-driven RPG I've played in years. What makes it so special is that every part of the game feels carefully crafted. The main story is emotional, gripping, and filled with unforgettable moments, but what truly surprised me was the quality of the side content. Unlike many open-world games where side quests feel like repetitive filler, Cyberpunk's side missions are so well-written and unique that they often feel like they could be part of the main storyline. Many of them introduce memorable characters, unexpected twists, and meaningful choices that make every mission worth playing.

The attention to detail is simply incredible. Night City is one of the most immersive worlds I've ever explored. Every district has its own identity, architecture, atmosphere, and people. The city constantly feels alive, with crowds walking the streets, traffic moving through highways, advertisements covering every building, and countless small details that make the world believable. Even the Badlands outside the city have their own unique atmosphere, making the contrast between the urban chaos and the empty desert feel natural and immersive.

Visually, Cyberpunk 2077 is absolutely stunning. The lighting, weather effects, reflections, animations, and overall art direction make almost every location look like it belongs in a sci-fi movie. Whether you're driving through the neon-lit streets at night or watching the sunrise over the Badlands, the game is full of breathtaking moments.

The RPG systems are another reason why I love this game. The skill tree gives you the freedom to create completely different builds depending on how you want to play. You can become a deadly Netrunner who hacks enemies from a distance, a stealth assassin using throwing knives and silenced weapons, a cyber-enhanced samurai with katanas, or a heavily armored tank charging into combat with shotguns and LMGs. Great game. Not quite on the level of Witcher 3 (the world and characters are just less diverse and interesting) but still well above par compared to most games. I’d highly recommend getting Phantom Liberty as it’s possibly better than the main story. What this game does best is the big missions/heists that feel very cinematic and action-packed. And of course the sheer detail of the environments is insane. Can’t say many of the characters have a great deal of depth, with the exception of Johnny and Reed who are genuinely well written and multi-faceted.

There’s a fairly solid progression system and ability to approach things different ways - unlike most games, many boss battles including the final boss can be beaten in stealth. I did however find that once I’d found the groove of my playstyle and a few key strong weapons it didn’t change up much after that. In an ideal world there’d be some more unique weapons/perks that allow for some goofy or niche playstyles late game, but I can’t complain too much as there is a fair degree of customisation and progression.

At points I did wish they did lean more into the cyberpunk world gameplay-wise e.g. having a drone companion, or a flying car, or something. At points it did feel like GTA with a futurist late-capitalist skin on it.

However overall, I can highly recommend! Looking forward to Projekt Red’s next game.

Cyberpunk 2077 is an absolutely phenomenal game, and what really makes it stand out is just how incredible its world is. Night City is one of the most impressive open worlds I've experienced. The sheer level of detail in the environment, from the towering skyscrapers and neon-lit streets to the crowded markets and back alleys, makes the city feel like a living, breathing place. Every district has its own identity, atmosphere, and personality. It's a world that genuinely makes you want to explore, even when you have no particular objective in mind.

The gunplay is another major highlight. Weapons feel impactful, combat is incredibly satisfying, and there's a great variety of weapons and approaches to engagements. Whether you're getting into a full-blown firefight, picking enemies off from a distance, or getting up close and personal, the combat is consistently fun.

The story is equally impressive. The writing, character development, dialogue, and world-building come together to create a genuinely memorable experience. The characters feel believable, the major story moments carry weight, and the narrative does an excellent job of keeping you invested from beginning to end.

There are a few minor glitches here and there, but they're easy to overlook considering everything else the game gets right.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is an incredible achievement. A beautifully realized open world, exceptionally enjoyable combat, and a fantastic story make this one of the best gaming experiences I've had. An easy 9.5/10.
